lesson.title: Antianxiety Medications: Turning Down an Overactive Alarm
lesson.summary: Antianxiety medications reduce excessive anxiety, most directly by enhancing the calming effect of GABA, the brain's primary inhibitory neurotransmitter, though different classes of these medications work in different ways and are typically used for different lengths of time.
lesson.body:
Antianxiety medications are used to reduce the physical and psychological symptoms of excessive, persistent anxiety, including but not limited to generalized anxiety disorder.

One well known class is benzodiazepines, which enhance the effect of GABA, the brain's main inhibitory neurotransmitter, at its receptor. Because GABA's role in the nervous system is to reduce the activity of the neurons it acts on, boosting its effect produces a calming, sedating effect relatively quickly. For this reason, benzodiazepines are often used for short-term or as-needed relief of acute anxiety. They also carry a risk of dependence with prolonged use, which is why they are generally prescribed cautiously and for limited periods rather than as an ongoing, open-ended treatment.

For longer-term management of anxiety disorders, certain antidepressant medications, particularly some SSRIs and SNRIs, are also commonly prescribed. These work more gradually than benzodiazepines but generally without the same dependence concerns. This illustrates that "antianxiety medication" is more of a functional category, medications used to treat anxiety, than a single, unified pharmacological class.

For many anxiety disorders, medication is often used alongside psychotherapy, such as cognitive-behavioral therapy, rather than as a stand-alone treatment. Therapy can directly address the thought patterns and avoidance behaviors that tend to maintain anxiety over time in ways that medication on its own does not, which is part of why combined treatment is common. As with the other medications discussed in this unit, decisions about whether and which antianxiety medication is appropriate for a given person are made with a qualified medical professional.
